releaseNotes: Hook installation becomes a contract instead of an instruction. The PostToolUse payload in templates/repo-agent-entrypoints/settings.json is the skill’s only automatic enforcement layer — it fires depth-check validators after artifact writes and blocks the screenshot grading pass — and scripts/fixtures/hooks.fixtures.ts already proved those commands behave correctly. What nothing proved was delivery: the sole install instruction was a prose line inside the template’s own JSON comment (“Copy this file to .claude/settings.json”), and zero of 60 validators referenced settings.json, so a generated business repo could pass every other gate with no enforcement running at all. New install:hooks merges the shipped entries into a target repo, replacing only entries this skill owns (marked _managed, with a legacy fallback matching pre-marker installs by command substring) while the founder’s own hooks, permissions, and env survive untouched; --write-skill-root records SKILL_ROOT so the hooks stop resolving to “.” and going quietly inactive. New check:hooks-installed (67 -> 68 checks) runs in two modes because a hollow pass is worse than no gate: template mode (what the audit runs) validates the shipped payload is well-formed and reinstallable, since the pipeline’s --root is templates/, which is not a business repo; business-repo mode (--root) reports missing settings, absent hooks, and command drift as errors carrying the one-line reinstall fix. scripts/lib/hook-contract.ts is the single source of truth all three consumers share — including a matcher-plus-status signature that deliberately excludes command text so an edited command reports as drift rather than as an absent hook plus a stray extra one. Nine round-trip fixtures plus LaunchBench scenario business-repo-hooks-not-installed; the drift fixture asserts the issue code rather than a bare exit 1, because a crashing validator also exits 1 and an earlier version of that fixture passed for exactly that wrong reason.

Plain language reaches the two pages founders actually open. A domain catalogue of all 447 tracked files found the skill’s own Always-On Contract (“never speak this file’s internal vocabulary to a founder”) being violated on its two most important founder-facing surfaces. launch-cockpit.html rendered the raw role id in visible body text (“Owner: orchestrator”) in the “Things I am watching” cards, outside any technical-details section: founder-copy.ts gains ownerCopy/ownerLabel — the same internal-id-to-plain-language pattern laneCopy, statusCopy, phaseCopy and modeCopy already use — and render-launch-cockpit.ts now renders “Handled by: Me, coordinating the work”. 11-star-experience.html carried internal shorthand in its title, h1, subtitle, section headings, an aria-label and a table header; it now speaks the plain vocabulary the cockpit already uses for the same concept (“The Standout Moment”). The root cause was in the gate itself: check-eleven-star-experience.ts required the HTML to contain “11-Star”, “Line Of Feasibility” and “V1 Scalable Slice” verbatim — mandating exactly the jargon SKILL.md forbids speaking to a founder — so the required phrases now name the four ideas in founder words while 11_STAR_EXPERIENCE.md keeps the precise internal vocabulary for the agent. The four archetype references drop their -lane suffix (ai-chat-companion.md, habit-tracker.md, photo-ai-media.md, social-network.md), rewritten across 18 files, freeing 40 bytes in SKILL.md.
